podcast.body: David Lee Roth is recognized for his "wailing lyrics," a signature element of Van Halen's sound during his tenure, exemplified in songs like "Running with the Devil." "What we do have is a classic Van Halen David Lee Roths wailing lyrics and a lot of great guitar riffs."

podcast.title: Replacement as Lead Singer
podcast.body: David Lee Roth was eventually replaced as the lead singer of Van Halen by Sammy Hagar. Despite this significant change, the band's loyal fanbase continued to support them. "when Van Halen starts relying a lot more on the synthesizer and also replace their lead singer with Sammy Heyghar they the fans tick with them."

xref.title: Three Lead Singers – David Lee Roth, Sammy Hagar, Gary Cherone; Eddie Van Halen Died October 6, 2020
xref.body: Van Halen has had three lead singers: David Lee Roth (1973–1984), Sammy Hagar (1985–1996), Roth briefly in late 1996, Gary Cherone of Extreme (1996–1999), Hagar again (2003–2005), and Roth from 2006 onward. A reunion tour with Roth was being planned when Eddie Van Halen was diagnosed with cancer; he died on October 6, 2020. "And then Eddie Van Halen got sick with cancer and eventually died on October 6, 2020."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Layne Staley's Vocal Style
xref.body: Layne Staley's voice and his harmonies with Jerry Cantrell were central to the band's sound, considered the best hard rock harmonies since David Lee Roth and Michael Anthony in Van Halen's early days. Their vocal arrangements often featured dual lead vocals, strategically overlapped, with the two voices typically separated by a major third. Staley, with the more powerful delivery, could transition from a menacing monotone to sharp, cutting explosions, and also had a great scream, appealing to both metal and alternative fans. "Technically, the two voices were separated by a major third with Lane having the more powerful of the two deliveries."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Reason for Rejecting Velvet Revolver Frontman Role
xref.body: Despite the musical chemistry and positive vibe during rehearsals, Ian Thorneley ultimately did not join Velvet Revolver. The band sought a "peacock" frontman in the vein of David Lee Roth or Scott Weiland, a role that didn't align with Ian's preference to play guitar on stage. "I'm not that comfortable doing the whole, you know, front guy tambourine thing. It's just not for me."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
